input.problem: Knowledge graph completion (KGC): predicting missing triples. The paper argues current LLM-based approaches encode graph context as flat text, failing to exploit graph structure, and lists three failures: structural information loss (prompts are long and noisy), static embeddings that do not adapt to query-specific structure, and generic LLM responses driven by pretraining data.
input.method: DrKGC. (1) Convert incomplete triples into natural-language questions with a template lexicon; (2) train a lightweight model to learn structural embeddings and mine logical rules; (3) use a bottom-up, rule-guided retrieval to extract a query-specific local subgraph; (4) apply a GCN adapter over the retrieved subgraph to produce local structural embeddings, which are integrated into the prompt for LLM fine-tuning. So graph context is used both to construct supervision and inside fine-tuning.
input.main_contribution: A dynamic subgraph retrieval-augmented LLM framework for KGC that combines mined logical rules, query-specific subgraph retrieval, and a GCN adapter for structure-aware LLM fine-tuning; claimed state of the art on general KGs and strong performance on domain-specific biomedical KGs with improved interpretability.
key_assumptions: Logical rules mined from the KG are predictive enough to guide subgraph retrieval.
A compact query-specific subgraph captures the structure needed for the prediction, without long or noisy text prompts.
A GCN adapter over the retrieved subgraph can inject structural information that the LLM cannot infer from text alone.
Restricting the LLM output space to candidates mitigates generic responses.
datasets: Two general-domain KG completion benchmark datasets (not named in the abstract)
Two biomedical KGs (not named in the abstract)
baselines: Not stated in abstract; related work contrasts KICGPT and KoPA-style generation-based methods
input.results: Abstract reports superior performance on two general-domain and two biomedical datasets. Full text limitations note fine-tuning is computationally intensive and performance is bounded by the underlying LLM and lightweight model.
limitations: Relies on fine-tuning large language models, which is computationally intensive.
Performance is inherently constrained by the capabilities of the LLM and the lightweight structural model.
input.code_availability: No code URL recorded for this paper (code_urls empty); GitHub tools unavailable in this investigation, so availability could not be verified.

relation_to_idea.basis: Problem overlap 0.55: both target reasoning that needs more than an isolated triple, but KGC vs. multi-hop KGQA differ. Method overlap 0.6: query-specific subgraph retrieval + LLM fine-tuning with graph context is the closest mechanism found, though not passage co-occurrence. Evaluation overlap 0.25: KGC benchmarks rather than KGQA WebQSP/CWQ/MetaQA.
relation_to_idea.conceptual_difference: DrKGC retrieves a query-specific subgraph at inference and injects it via a GCN adapter into an LLM prompt for KGC, guided by mined logical rules. The idea instead enriches the *training supervision signal* for KGQA with triples co-occurring in the same source passage, and studies isolated-vs-context regimes plus a repair loop. Same intuition (local context beyond an isolated triple) but different task (completion vs. QA), different context source (rule-guided graph retrieval vs. passage provenance), and different stage (inference+adapter vs. supervision construction).

input.problem: RAG for KGQA: recent approaches rely on costly LLM calls to generate executable relation paths or traverse the KG, which is inefficient for complex questions (multi-hop, multi-entity).
input.method: GNN-RAG. A lightweight GNN scores KG nodes by question relevance and neighbour relevance; shortest paths connecting question entities to GNN answer candidates are retrieved, verbalized, and given to the LLM as context. Additional retrieval-augmentation and routing techniques improve end-to-end efficiency.
input.main_contribution: Lightweight GNN-based graph retrieval for KGQA that lets a 7B tuned LLM match or outperform GPT-4, improving complex (multi-hop/multi-entity) answering by 8.9-15.5 F1 points over LLM-based retrieval while using 9x fewer KG tokens and no extra LLM calls for retrieval.
key_assumptions: The retrieved question-specific subgraph contains the answer nodes.
Entity linking from the question to KG entities is correct.
Shortest paths from question entities to GNN answer candidates are an adequate verbalized context for the LLM.
baselines: No RAG, KG-RAG variants, long-context inference, GPT-4 (as cited in the abstract)
input.results: Effective retrieval on WebQSP and CWQ; 8.9-15.5 F1 improvement on multi-hop and multi-entity questions over LLM-based retrieval; 9x fewer KG tokens than long-context inference; matches or beats GPT-4 with a 7B tuned LLM.
limitations: Assumes the KG subgraph the GNN reasons over contains the answer nodes, which may fail for some questions or under entity-linking errors.
Uses simple prompting with shortest paths from question entities to candidate answers as context.
input.code_availability: Code stated as https://github.com/cmavro/GNN-RAG in the abstract; repository inspection unavailable in this investigation.

relation_to_idea.basis: Problem overlap 0.7: both are multi-hop KGQA over the same benchmarks. Method overlap 0.55: retrieval of paths/subgraphs as LLM context is adjacent but is inference-time and path-based, not passage-derived training supervision. Evaluation overlap 0.85: identical WebQSP/CWQ benchmarks and answer-F1-style metrics.
relation_to_idea.conceptual_difference: GNN-RAG builds the supporting context (shortest paths) at inference time and feeds it to a frozen/lightly tuned LLM; the supervision used to train the GNN is question-answer pairs, not context-enriched triples. The idea instead attaches co-passage triples to each training supervision signal and compares isolated vs. context regimes, then adds a repair loop and lower-hop RL. Both supply multi-hop context, but one is retrieval-time context construction and the other is training-time supervision enrichment.

input.problem: Multi-hop KBQA suffers from missing supervision at intermediate reasoning steps. Models receive feedback only from the final answer, making learning unstable or ineffective, and a correct answer can be reached by a spurious relation path.
input.method: Teacher-student approach. The student network finds answer entities; the teacher network learns intermediate entity distributions using both forward and backward reasoning to produce more reliable intermediate supervision signals and alleviate spurious reasoning. Backward reasoning is what makes the teacher's intermediate signals more reliable.
input.main_contribution: Shown, to the authors' knowledge, as the first explicit learning of intermediate supervision signals with a teacher-student framework for multi-hop KBQA, with bidirectional (forward+backward) reasoning for more reliable intermediate signals; effective especially when training data is limited.
key_assumptions: Question-answer pairs are available but ground-truth relation paths are not (as stated for KGQA in GNN-RAG, and consistent here).
Intermediate entity distributions can be learned by a teacher without explicit path labels.
Bidirectional reasoning produces less spurious intermediate supervision than forward-only reasoning.
A question-specific subgraph containing the answer can be constructed (coverage 94.9% WebQSP, 79.3% CWQ, ~99-100% MetaQA per Table 1 statistics quoted in text).
datasets: WebQuestionsSP (WebQSP; 4737 questions, up to 2-hop over Freebase)
baselines: Not extracted from the passages retrieved; the abstract claims effectiveness on three benchmark datasets
metrics: Not confirmed from the passages retrieved; the paper reports standard multi-hop KBQA final-answer evaluation on three benchmark datasets
input.results: Reports effectiveness on the KBQA task on three benchmark datasets, especially in cases lacking training data.
limitations: Not stated in abstract (no limitations section was located in the extracted outline)
input.code_availability: No code URL recorded for this paper; GitHub tools unavailable in this investigation. The paper is the NSM (Neural State Machine) teacher-student work.

relation_to_idea.basis: Problem overlap 0.85: same multi-hop KGQA setting, same spurious-intermediate-reasoning concern, same lack of intermediate supervision. Method overlap 0.4: intermediate supervision learning is a different intervention from enriching the input with co-passage context. Evaluation overlap 0.9: identical benchmark suite (MetaQA/WebQSP/CWQ).
relation_to_idea.conceptual_difference: NSM addresses *where the supervisory signal comes from* by learning intermediate entity distributions, keeping the input triple/path structure unchanged. The idea addresses *what context accompanies a given supervision signal* by adding co-passage triples. NSM's motivation (spurious paths caused by absent intermediate supervision) is closely aligned with the idea's stated reliability concern, but its mechanism (teacher-student bidirectional reasoning) is different from context-subgraph enrichment and from a one-hop error repair loop.

input.problem: KBQA requires accurate multi-hop reasoning, but existing approaches perform sequential reasoning steps guided by predefined pipelines, restricting flexibility and causing error cascades due to isolated reasoning at each step.
input.method: KG-Hopper: an RL framework that trains a compact open reasoning LLM to perform integrated multi-hop KG reasoning in a single inference round, embedding the entire KG traversal and decision process into a unified 'thinking' stage, enabling global reasoning over cross-step dependencies and dynamic path exploration with backtracking.
input.main_contribution: A compact (7B) open RL-trained reasoning LLM that matches or beats larger multi-step systems (up to 70B) and is competitive with GPT-3.5-Turbo/GPT-4o-mini on eight KG reasoning benchmarks, while remaining data-efficient, with public code.
key_assumptions: Multi-step reasoning can be internalized into a single thinking stage of a reasoning LLM.
RL over the KG traversal yields better global coherence than fixed pipelines.
Cross-step dependencies matter, so isolating each step is harmful.
datasets: Eight KG reasoning benchmarks (names not stated in abstract)
benchmarks: Eight KG reasoning benchmarks (names not stated in abstract)
baselines: Larger multi-step systems up to 70B parameters
metrics: Not stated in abstract (KG reasoning benchmark metrics)
input.results: A 7B KG-Hopper consistently outperforms larger multi-step systems up to 70B and is competitive with GPT-3.5-Turbo and GPT-4o-mini, while remaining compact, open and data-efficient.
input.code_availability: Code stated as https://github.com/Wangshuaiia/KG-Hopper in the abstract; repository inspection unavailable in this investigation.

relation_to_idea.basis: Problem overlap 0.7: same multi-hop KG reasoning over KGs and the same 'isolated steps are harmful' diagnosis. Method overlap 0.5: RL on LLMs for KG reasoning overlaps with the idea's RL stage, but not with context-enriched triple supervision. Evaluation overlap 0.6: KG reasoning benchmarks overlap but not confirmed KGQA benchmarks.
relation_to_idea.conceptual_difference: KG-Hopper is an RL training framework that removes step isolation by internalizing traversal in the LLM's thinking stage; it does not change the supervision context of individual triples. The idea's third component (RL on lower-hop instances for deeper-hop transfer) is directly comparable, so KG-Hopper is a strong baseline/threat for that component rather than for the context-subgraph component.

input.problem: LLMs hallucinate on domain-specific and reasoning-heavy tasks; multi-hop question answering over a knowledge graph needs the right subgraph, and naive RAG is insufficient.
input.method: SG-RAG MOT: uses Cypher queries to search the KG and retrieve the necessary subgraph (SG-RAG), then adds a Merging and Ordering Triplets (MOT) step that hierarchically merges retrieved subgraphs to reduce triplet redundancy and orders triplets along a BFS traversal before presentation to the LLM.
input.main_contribution: Evidence that merging overlapping retrieved subgraphs (up to a point) and imposing an order on the retrieved triplets improves answer precision over Chain-of-Thought and Graph Chain-of-Thought on MetaQA.
key_assumptions: The relevant subgraph is retrievable via Cypher queries from the KG.
Redundancy in retrieved triplets hurts; merging and BFS ordering help.
The LLM can exploit merged, ordered triplets as context.
metrics: Not stated in abstract (accuracy of answers)
input.results: SG-RAG MOT gives more accurate answers than Chain-of-Thought and Graph Chain-of-Thought on MetaQA; merging highly overlapping subgraphs (up to some point) and ordering triplets helps the LLM generate more precise answers.
input.code_availability: No code URL recorded; GitHub tools unavailable in this investigation.

relation_to_idea.basis: Problem overlap 0.75: multi-hop KGQA over subgraphs, same MetaQA benchmark. Method overlap 0.6: subgraph triplets as LLM context plus merging/ordering is mechanistically close to context-subgraph construction. Evaluation overlap 0.7: shared MetaQA but no training-time regime comparison.
relation_to_idea.conceptual_difference: SG-RAG MOT constructs and orders a subgraph of triplets at inference time to condition an LLM's answer; it does not train the model, does not use source-passage provenance, and has no repair loop or RL stage. The idea's context-subgraph idea is similar in spirit (triplets beyond the path, merged and ordered) but applied to the training supervision signal rather than to prompting, which is the key distinction.

Reducing sparsity via embeddings substitutes for external text.
input.main_contribution: First exploration of KG embedding methods for multi-hop KGQA; EmbedKGQA is particularly effective on sparse KGs and removes the hard answer-selection-from-neighborhood constraint.
input.method: EmbedKGQA: uses knowledge base embedding methods (designed for missing link prediction) to reduce KG sparsity for multi-hop KGQA, and relaxes the requirement that answers be selected from a pre-specified neighborhood (a sub-optimal constraint enforced by previous multi-hop KGQA methods).
input.problem: Multi-hop KGQA must reason over multiple edges of a KG, but KGs are often incomplete with many missing links, which is especially challenging for multi-hop questions. Prior work handles KG sparsity using relevant external text, which is not always available.

relation_to_idea.basis: Problem overlap 0.8: multi-hop KGQA over incomplete KGs. Method overlap 0.3: KG embeddings handle sparsity at the representation level, not by adding context to the supervision signal. Evaluation overlap 0.7: shared benchmark family.
relation_to_idea.conceptual_difference: EmbedKGQA addresses KG incompleteness with embeddings and removes neighborhood-constrained answer selection; it does not enrich supervision with context triples, nor repair one-hop failures, nor use RL over hop depths. It is relevant as a baseline for the idea's claim that base-fact unreliability harms multi-hop QA, since it is an alternative remedy (embedding-based link prediction) already established for sparsity.

input.results: Extensive experiments on multiple benchmark datasets demonstrate effectiveness over other state-of-the-art baselines.

input.code_availability: Code for experiments released (per abstract footnote); no repository URL recorded in this record and GitHub tools unavailable in this investigation.
key_assumptions: A relevant subgraph can be extracted from the external KG for each question.
Multi-hop, multi-relational reasoning over that subgraph improves a pretrained LM's QA.
Path-based reasoning and GNNs can be unified without loss of scalability or interpretability.
input.main_contribution: A multi-hop relational reasoning module over extracted KG subgraphs that unifies path-based reasoning and GNNs, improving interpretability and scalability, with effectiveness shown on CommonsenseQA and OpenbookQA.
input.method: MHGRN (multi-hop graph relation network): a knowledge-aware approach that equips pretrained language models with a multi-hop relational reasoning module performing multi-hop, multi-relational reasoning over subgraphs extracted from external knowledge graphs. The module unifies path-based reasoning methods and graph neural networks for interpretability and scalability.
input.problem: Existing work that augments QA models with external knowledge such as knowledge graphs either struggles to model multi-hop relations efficiently or lacks transparency into the model's prediction rationale.

relation_to_idea.basis: Problem overlap 0.5: knowledge-aware multi-hop reasoning but commonsense QA rather than KGQA over Freebase. Method overlap 0.45: reasoning over KG subgraphs with a pretrained LM is adjacent, but the module is architectural and inference-time. Evaluation overlap 0.15: CommonsenseQA/OpenbookQA differ from MetaQA/WebQSP/CWQ.
relation_to_idea.conceptual_difference: MHGRN adds a relational reasoning module that consumes an extracted KG subgraph at inference; it does not change training supervision to include co-passage context, and has no repair loop or RL. It is evidence that subgraph context helps knowledge-aware QA, which supports the idea's premise, but the mechanism and benchmarks are distinct.

input.results: Effectiveness and scalability shown empirically on CommonsenseQA and OpenbookQA, with case studies interpreting behaviour.

input.resolution: Partially resolved: the standard multi-hop KGQA benchmarks are structured-KG benchmarks. NSM's full text states that WebQSP questions are 'answerable using Freebase as the knowledge base', and CWQ is generated from WebQSP, so neither carries source passages from which co-passage triples could be drawn; MetaQA is a synthetic movie KG. Therefore the mechanism cannot be evaluated on the standard benchmark suite without (a) switching to text-grounded KGs with provenance or (b) redefining context as graph neighbourhood, which is largely covered by subgraph retrieval work. A targeted search for provenance-bearing / text-derived KGs with co-passage triples is still needed.

input.confidence_basis: Based on full-text reads of DrKGC and GNN-RAG and abstracts of GRAG/SG-RAG/UniKGQA; a targeted search for training-time multi-triple supervision was not yet run.
input.resolution: Partially resolved: the closest retrieved subgraph-augmentation work constructs context at inference time (GNN-RAG retrieves shortest paths for prompt context; SG-RAG MOT merges/orders retrieved triplets; GRAG retrieves textual subgraphs) or learns a query-specific subgraph at inference with a GCN adapter integrated into a prompt during LLM fine-tuning (DrKGC). None of them derives context from the source passage of the supervision triple. So context-subgraph retrieval per se is not novel, but passage-derived, training-supervision-level context enrichment was not found in the retrieved set. The distinction from DrKGC is narrow and must be argued explicitly.
